title: taskAuditRecord
responsibility: Persists a content-addressed audit of the task, source revision, individual checks and remaining semantic limitation.

inputs.name: taskAuditRecord.root
inputs.description: Project filesystem root that is the working directory of the Git probe `rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path harness/task-audits` and whose resolved path is hashed to name the temporary fallback directory. The root is not checked for existence or repository status here, and a probe failure or empty result selects the temporary fallback.

inputs.name: taskAuditRecord.input
inputs.type: TaskAuditInput & { commit: string | null; checks: TaskCheck[] }
inputs.description: Declared task (kind and goal, plus optional plan, loop and units), the commit to record or null, and the individual check outcomes to persist. Units are de-duplicated and sorted, the checks array is stored unchanged, and passed is derived as true only when at least one check exists and every check passed.

examples.goal: Plan retries for the webhook consumer

checks.detail: Provide a substantive overview section, including an explicit explanation when none applies.

examples.goal: Persist task audits under a content-addressed id
Persist task audits under a content-addressed id

checks.detail: Task evidence could not be read.

outputs.name: taskAuditRecord
outputs.description: The resolved TaskAudit, whose id is the SHA-256 hex digest of the JSON serialization of every field except id. It is returned only after `<id>.json` is written to the Git-path or temporary fallback directory, and the returned object does not report that location.

errors.name: NodeJS.ErrnoException
errors.description: Filesystem failure rejected by the `mkdir` call (with `recursive: true`) that creates the audit directory or by the `writeFile` call that writes `<id>.json`. Nothing in the function catches it, so the rejection reaches the caller and no audit is returned.
